AWPTCM-T43868.objective:
• An SNMPv1 community configured on the device with read-only access rights, present in running configuration and surviving a restart of the SNMP agent.
  • An SNMPv1 community configured with read-write access rights, distinct from the read-only community and independently addressable by a manager.
  • SNMP agent enabled, listening for v1 protocol messages, and reachable from a manager on a routed and a directly attached interface.
  • A successful SNMPv1 GET of a scalar system object returning the device's own value for that object.
  • A successful SNMPv1 GET-NEXT and full walk of a subtree, returning objects in lexicographic order and terminating cleanly at the end of the MIB view.
  • A successful SNMPv1 SET of a writable object using the read-write community, with the new value observable both through a subsequent GET and through the device's own management interface.
  • Interface, system and SNMP-statistics MIB objects readable over v1 with values consistent with the device's operational state.
  • A SET attempted with a read-only community rejected, with the object's value unchanged afterwards.
  • A request carrying an unconfigured or misspelled community name rejected, with no varbind data returned to the requester.
  • A request from a host excluded by the community's associated access list rejected, while the same request from a permitted host succeeds.
  • An access list referenced by a community that names a host address parsed correctly at configuration time and at agent start-up, with no configuration-file read error and no loss of the community entry.
  • An access list referenced by a community but not yet defined handled deterministically, with the resulting permit/deny behaviour stated and stable across a restart.
  • A GET of a non-existent object identifier answered with the v1-appropriate error condition rather than a silent or malformed response.
  • A SET of a read-only object, or of a value outside the object's permitted range or type, rejected with the v1-appropriate error condition and the stored value unchanged.
  • A response whose contents would exceed the transport's message size handled without agent failure and without truncated or corrupt varbinds.
  • The configured maximum number of v1 communities accepted, with an attempt to add one beyond the maximum refused and the existing communities left intact.
  • Community names accepted across the supported length and character range, and names outside it refused at configuration time.
  • v1 access unaffected by the presence of v2c communities and v3 users configured concurrently, with each version answering only its own requests.
  • Removal of a community immediately denying further requests that use it, with no cached authorisation permitting a subsequent request.
  • SNMP agent disabled resulting in no response to a previously working v1 request, and re-enabling restoring access without reconfiguration.
  • v1 access available on a virtual chassis stack through the stack's management address, served identically regardless of which member is the active master.
  • v1 access preserved across a master failover in a stack, with the community set and access lists intact on the new master.
  • Per-member and stack-wide objects distinguishable in a v1 walk of a stacked device, reporting the true membership of the stack.
  • SNMP input, output, error and authentication-failure counters incrementing in step with the requests and rejections generated.
  • An authentication failure recorded — as a counter and, where enabled, as a trap or log entry — identifying the event without disclosing the offered community name in clear text.
  • Show output for SNMP configuration listing each community with its access rights and any associated access list, matching the running configuration.
  • Log entries for agent start, stop and configuration change present and timestamped consistently with the actions performed.
  • No SNMP-related process restart, memory growth or system message indicating fault after sustained walk, get and set activity.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Set an SNMPv1 community with read-only access rights and verify it appears in the running configuration with the correct access rights.
Restart the SNMP agent and confirm the read-only community is still present and still usable without reconfiguration.
Set a second SNMPv1 community with read-write access rights, distinct from the read-only community, and confirm both entries coexist in the running configuration.
Verify the SNMP agent is enabled and listening for v1 protocol messages.
Test with a manager on a directly attached interface and confirm the device answers SNMPv1 requests.
Test with a manager reachable over a routed interface and confirm the device answers SNMPv1 requests on that path as well.
Verify an SNMPv1 GET of a scalar system object returns the device's own configured value for that object.
Verify an SNMPv1 GET-NEXT returns the lexicographic successor of the requested object identifier.
Perform a full SNMPv1 walk of a subtree and confirm objects are returned in lexicographic order and the walk terminates cleanly at the end of the MIB view.
steps.expectedResult: No repeated, out-of-order or looping varbinds.

steps.description: Verify an SNMPv1 SET of a writable object using the read-write community succeeds, and confirm the new value with a subsequent GET.
Confirm the value written by SNMP is also observable through the device's own management interface.
Verify interface MIB objects are readable over v1 and that reported state, speed and counters are consistent with the interfaces' operational state.
Verify system MIB objects are readable over v1 and consistent with the device's configured identity and uptime.
Verify SNMP-statistics MIB objects are readable over v1 and reflect the traffic the manager has generated.
Test with an SNMPv1 SET issued using the read-only community and confirm it is rejected.
steps.expectedResult: Request refused and the object's value is unchanged afterwards.

steps.description: Test with a request carrying an unconfigured or misspelled community name and confirm it is rejected with no varbind data returned to the requester.
Associate an access list with a community, then test with a request from a host excluded by that access list and confirm it is rejected.
Test with the same request from a host permitted by the access list and confirm it succeeds.
Verify an access list that names a host address and is referenced by a community is parsed correctly at configuration time and again at agent start-up.
steps.expectedResult: No configuration-file read error and no loss of the community entry.

steps.description: Configure a community that references an access list which has not yet been defined, and confirm the resulting permit or deny behaviour is deterministic and documented.
Restart the device or the SNMP agent and confirm the behaviour of the community with the undefined access list is unchanged.
Verify a GET of a non-existent object identifier is answered with the v1-appropriate error condition rather than a silent or malformed response.
Verify a SET of a read-only object is rejected with the v1-appropriate error condition and the stored value is unchanged.
Verify a SET carrying a value outside the object's permitted range, or of the wrong type, is rejected with the v1-appropriate error condition and the stored value is unchanged.
Request a response whose contents would exceed the transport's message size and confirm the agent handles it without failing and without returning truncated or corrupt varbinds.
Configure the supported maximum number of v1 communities and confirm all are accepted and usable.
Attempt to add one community beyond the supported maximum and confirm it is refused with the existing communities left intact.
Verify community names are accepted across the supported length and character range.
Verify community names outside the supported length or character range are refused at configuration time.
Configure v2c communities and v3 users concurrently with the v1 communities and confirm v1 access is unaffected.
Test with requests of each version and confirm each version answers only its own requests.
Remove a community and confirm further requests using that community are denied immediately, with no cached authorisation permitting a subsequent request.
Disable the SNMP agent and confirm a previously working v1 request receives no response.
Re-enable the SNMP agent and confirm v1 access is restored without reconfiguration.
On a virtual chassis stack, verify v1 access through the stack's management address is served identically regardless of which member is the active master.
Force a master failover on the stack and confirm v1 access is preserved with the community set and access lists intact on the new master.
Walk a stacked device over v1 and confirm per-member and stack-wide objects are distinguishable and report the true membership of the stack.
Verify the SNMP input, output, error and authentication-failure counters increment in step with the requests and rejections generated during this test.
Confirm an authentication failure is recorded as a counter and, where enabled, as a trap or log entry identifying the event.
steps.expectedResult: The offered community name is not disclosed in clear text.

steps.description: Verify the show output for SNMP configuration lists each community with its access rights and any associated access list, matching the running configuration.
Confirm log entries exist for SNMP agent start, stop and configuration change, timestamped consistently with the actions performed.
After sustained walk, get and set activity, confirm no SNMP-related process restart, memory growth or system message indicating fault.
